root_motivation: WHO: an agent that knows the job (a scheduled job, a webhook inbox, uptime probes, a table, docs Q&A) and its user. WHAT: host.template_apply(name) provisions the whole job -- tools, tables, triggers -- in one all-or-nothing call and returns the demo call that shows the first result. WHY: the unit an agent wants is the job, not the tool; assembling a scheduled job from primitives takes three calls (publish, trigger set, call) and the 10-09 recipe sessions took 7 to 13.
user_persona: An agent on a fresh free tenant that calls host.template_list or GET /templates.json to pick a template, host.template_apply(name="scheduled-job"), runs the returned demo.call and shows its user the job's first result in two calls; and later host.template_remove to undo it without losing what the user changed.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh free tenant and a test call log, When host.template_apply(name="scheduled-job") runs and then the returned demo.call runs, Then a result equal to demo.expect is in the second call's result and the log holds exactly 2 calls; a third required call fails the test (premise falsified).

Given templates/*.toml, When cargo test ttpl_drift runs, Then every kind, spec field, demo tool and next verb resolves against the registry and host_tools, and a fixture template with kind = "webhook" fails naming the file and field.

Given a free tenant already holding 3 event triggers, When webhook-inbox is applied, Then the error is plan_limit with data.ceiling == "event_triggers_max" and the tenant's tool, table and trigger counts are unchanged.
Given a tool create that fails midway (planted invalid spec in a test template), When apply runs, Then the response is the create's error and no object tagged with that template remains.

Given an applied template, When applied again with the same name, Then no duplicate tool, table or trigger exists, updated lists the objects, and the tool's version advanced by one; Given two concurrent applies, Then one succeeds and one returns conflict with data.retry_after_s.

Given anonymous and keyed host.template_list and GET /templates.json, When called, Then all three return the same five names with one_line, creates counts and plan_fit, and keyed host.quickstart without kind carries templates.
Given an applied template whose tool the user republished, When host.template_remove runs, Then the trigger and table are removed, the tool is kept and named under kept.

Given prod after this lands, When the public listing is fetched, Then it names at least five templates (Live; evidence: curl -s https://mcphost.dev/templates.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys;n=len(json.load(sys.stdin)["templates"]);print(n);sys.exit(0 if n>=5 else 1)')
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: curl -s https://mcphost.dev/templates.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys;n=len(json.load(sys.stdin)["templates"]);print(n);sys.exit(0 if n>=5 else 1)')

scope: src/templates.rs (templates, apply, remove, list, drift check, per-tenant lock); templates/*.toml (five templates); migrations/0143_template_objects.sql (template_objects tags); src/db.rs (tag methods); src/webhook_inbox.rs and src/uptime.rs reused in process; descriptors, dispatch arms, write_verbs rows, output schemas, GET /templates.json, quickstart.templates and the generated contracts, docs, SDKs and llms.txt.
non_goals: User-authored templates (host.template_apply source=, P2); templates that need secrets the host cannot ask for (the response names secrets_required and stops); changing host.webhook_inbox.create, host.uptime.create or host.example.fork; generating templates from recipes/*.toml (hand-written here); the AC 8 prod read (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.wrap_not_replace: webhook-inbox and uptime-probes call host.webhook_inbox.create and host.uptime.create in process; they do not replace them.
additional.all_or_nothing: A failed create removes every object the call made; plan ceilings are checked before any create.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent need several calls to show a job's first result?
five_whys_trace.a: host.tool_publish creates one tool; the trigger and the demo call are separate steps.
The host exposes primitives; nothing composes tools, tables and triggers into a job.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can a template compose them in one call?
five_whys_trace.a: The host already knows every piece: the kind registry, the plan ceilings and the in-process handlers behind publish, table create and trigger set.

five_whys_trace.q: Why data files and a drift test?
five_whys_trace.a: Templates are reviewable data; a PR that names a kind or verb the registry lacks must fail CI, not an agent's call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why tag every object and lock per tenant?
five_whys_trace.a: Rollback, re-apply and remove must act on exactly what a template made, and two applies on one tenant must not race.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a template that needs a secret stop before create or create and mark needs_secret?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: It stops before any create and names secrets_required; the five shipped templates need none today.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should scheduled-job take the tool source as a param or wrap an existing tool?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: It ships its own jq tool in tools[], so apply works on a fresh tenant.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which tool kind does scheduled-job use?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: jq: it runs in process with no sandbox, so the demo call returns demo.expect deterministically.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What does unmodified since apply mean for remove?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: A tool whose active version still equals the one tagged, a table whose row count still equals the count tagged, and a trigger still firing the tagged tool; anything else is kept.
